_doc: Revert-verify mutants for #4376 (sh:domain applicability cached per class set + getAllShapes hoisted out of the per-subject loop). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py packages/core/tests/services/shape-applicability-4376.spec.json after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute; the driver copies the tree with node_modules symlinked, splices one mutation into the copy's ShaclLiteValidator.ts and runs the validator suite; `expect` names the axes that MUST go red). Axis keys are the S<N> prefixes of the it() titles — `red_re` reads them; the file's other suites use T<N>/V<N>, so S is free.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/ShaclLiteValidator.ts

M1_getAllShapes_not_hoisted._note: Undoes the hoist alone — the cache still works, so only the materialisation count moves. S1 is the sole axis that can see it, which is why S1 asserts a COUNT rather than an outcome.

M2_cache_never_hits._note: Lookup key can never match, so applicability is recomputed for every subject while the write path and the verdicts stay correct. Only the counting axes see it — the same shape as M1 in the #4369 spec.

M3_key_conflates_different_class_sets._note: Keys on the SIZE of the class set, so two different single-class subjects share an entry and the second inherits the first's verdict. This is the mutant that matters: a too-coarse key is the way this optimisation turns into a correctness bug. S4 joins the measured set because its three subjects no longer share one key either (two of them carry two classes, the third three).

M4_key_keeps_order_and_duplicates._note: Same anchor as M3, different splice — the driver applies each mutant to a pristine copy, so sharing an anchor is fine. Drops the sort and the de-duplication, splitting one logical class set across three cache entries.

M5_domainless_shapes_stop_applying._note: Guards the branch that makes a shape with an empty sh:domain apply to every subject — including subjects with no resolvable class, which is the only population S5 can distinguish it on.

M6_subclass_path_dropped_from_the_filter._note: Without this mutant S6 was green under every other one — vacuous. It removes the hierarchy consultation from the cached filter, so only an EXACT class match applies; S6's subject is a subclass of the domain, and S2's ask-list becomes empty. S4 is in the measured set as well — its ask-list also empties, which I predicted as [S2, S6] and corrected against the run rather than the other way round.
